Subject: NexaHealth DPA / subprocessor locality questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — NexaHealth is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. Legal and InfoSec asked me to follow up with a few items before we can sign the DPA:

- We need a current subprocessor inventory with geographic locations (US onshore vs offshore).
- For the CPRA/CCPA service-provider classification, can you confirm Redwood will not act as a controller or sell consumer data and will adhere to limited-use obligations?
- We have an onshore fallback requirement for regulated workflows: if offshore subprocessors are used, we need an onshore fallback plan and an estimated RTO for failing over to US-only processors.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report or attestations and encryption-at-rest proof (keys and KMS zoning).

I’ve attached the redlined DPA our counsel sent (NexaHealth_DPA_redline.pdf). Can you send a quick mapping and proposed plan by next week?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that helps.

—Sam

Head of Integrations, NexaHealth

Subject: Re: Fwd: NexaHealth DPA / subprocessor locality questions

Karthik / team — quick legal/security take after an initial pass. Notes below that I want to include in the response to Sam:

1) Service provider / limited-use: Redwood is comfortable confirming we act as a "service provider / processor" under CPRA/CCPA. We will not sell personal data and our permitted use is explicitly limited to delivering inference and telemetry needed to operate the service. Suggested language: "Redwood Inference shall process personal information solely on behalf of Customer and for the purposes set forth in the Agreement. Redwood will not sell, retain, use, or disclose personal information for any purpose other than providing the Services, unless required by law."

2) Subprocessor inventory: Neha can share a CSV with subprocessors and country listed. We should highlight which subprocessors support US-only routing or have onshore alternatives. I recommend we proactively offer a mapping: (a) primary subprocessor + location; (b) whether they support onshore fallback; (c) estimated RTO in business hours for fallback.

3) Onshore fallback obligations: Their redline attempts to mandate an immediate shift to US-based processors upon request. We should propose a middle-ground: an onshore-fallback "plan" with committed timelines and cost/lead time. Example: initial remap within 48-72 hours for critical workflows where we control routing (edge/region routing), or a longer provisioning window (up to 14 days) when new capacity needs to be deployed. Include an SLA for data cutover and an annual test. Avoid open-ended indemnities or financial penalties tied to staff-level subprocessors.

4) Evidence: SOC 2 report link plus a short KMS note. We can provide SOC2 attestation under NDA (link provided in response). For KMS: we encrypt at rest using AES-256 and support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we use HSM-backed KMS with region zoning. We should attach a short "onshore_fallback_summary.pdf" that outlines the technical steps and timelines.

I attached a redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (internal copy) and a one-page onshore_fallback_summary.pdf draft. I can prepare suggested DPA language to counter their redline — Laura, can you draft the suggested edits to push back on the immediate-shift clause?

—Olga
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: onshore_fallback_summary.pdf (PDF)]

Hi Sam / Maya — thanks for sending the redline. Quick response and attached materials:

Summary: Redwood confirms we operate as a Service Provider/Processor under US state privacy laws (CPRA/CCPA) and will not sell consumer data.

What we attached for you:
- redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv — full inventory with country column and a "US-onshore-available" flag.
- onshore_fallback_summary.pdf — outlines fallback options, routing controls, timing expectations and a proposed annual test cadence.
- SOC2 attestation link (we can send the PDF via NDA if needed): https://redwood-internal.company/soc2-report

Key points:
- Service-provider language: we propose the clause Olga suggested (see quoted text below).
- Onshore fallback: we cannot accept an immediate-mandate to move production workloads within 24 hours across all possible subprocessors. Instead we propose: for regulated workflows where routing is under our control, Redwood will enable US-only routing within 48-72 business hours where capacity exists. Where new capacity or contractual onboarding is required, our commitment is to remediate within 14 calendar days, with formal notification and a test plan. For Dedicated/Private customers we already support region-pinning and BYOK.
- RTO examples we provided in the inventory for each subprocessor (e.g., PartnerX: US fallback available, 24–48 hours; PartnerY: requires contract + reprovisioning, 10–14 days).
- KMS & encryption: Hosted: AES-256 at rest, HSM-backed keys, customer-specific key separation; Dedicated/Private: optional customer-managed KMS.

Next steps I propose:
1) If the above is acceptable, we can provide a narrow DPA revision that preserves their limited-use ask and substitutes our fallback timelines for the immediate-shift language.
2) Offer a 30-minute technical sync (I can coordinate with Ben) to walk through the inventory and the plan.

Quoted suggested service-provider sentence (from Olga):
"Redwood Inference shall process personal information solely on behalf of Customer and for the purposes set forth in the Agreement. Redwood will not sell, retain, use, or disclose personal information for any purpose other than providing the Services, unless required by law."

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv, onshore_fallback_summary.pdf

Let us know a good time for the sync or if you'd prefer a written DPA counter with our redlines.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV)]
